To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
at least five of eight regions of sequence similarity between E1 of BPV-1 and T-ag of SV40 that are thought to confer helicase activity are required for E1 to support DNA replication in vivo.

(i) E1 and T-antigen share eight regions of sequence similarity, seven of which are important for E2TA-dependent DNA replication, and (ii) E1 and E2TA share a region of sequence similarity that is important for E2-dependent transcriptional transactivation and for E2TA-E1 association.
the regions of E1 similar to T-ag that are required for DNA binding and helicase activity are not required for E1 to act as a negative regulator of E2TA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional analysis of a region of similarity between E2TA and T-ag.
identifying the functions of specific regions of E1 that are necessary for its ability to support viral DNA replication and to inhibit transcription.
the identification and analysis of regions of similarity between two multifunctional DNA replication proteins, BPV-1 and SV40 E1 and T-antigen, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the regions of similarity between the DNA helicase domains of E1 and T are important for E2-dependent DNA replication and that these regions are not essential for E2-dependent transcription inhibition.

the eight regions of E1 that are homologous to regions in T-antigen are not all functionally important for E1 to support BPV-1 DNA replication in vivo, nor are they functionally important for the inhibition of E2-dependent transcription.
the E1 regions of similarity to T-ag are important for E2TA-dependent DNA replication and E1-dependent transcriptional inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the E1 protein is a multifunction protein whose properties include DNA binding to the origin of replication, ATP binding, ATP hydrolysis, and helicase activity; these properties may be required for E1's roles in viral DNA replication and inhibition of E2-mediated transcriptional transactivation.
the eight regions of sequence similarity between E1 of BPV-1 and T-ag of SV40 are not all functionally equivalent.
the regions in BPV- 1 E1 that are most similar to regions in SV40 T-ag are important for DNA replication but are not required for E1's capacity to act as a repressor of E2TA- dependent transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that

E1 has at least two distinct functional activities, DNA replication and transcriptional inhibition, which are separable in that the E1 mutants defective in supporting DNA replication can still inhibit E2TA.

the regions of similarity in E1 that correspond to regions in T-antigen that confer DNA helicase function are important for E2TA-dependent viral DNA replication but not for E1's capacity to act in trans to inhibit E2-dependent transcription.
E1's DNA replication function and its ability to inhibit E2-dependent transcription can be dissociated.
